title: Gehenna Cults
summary: Secret circles of Camarilla elders who fear the end.

claims.text: Officially the Camarilla calls Gehenna a tale to scare childer, but some elders fear it more than the young do, since their old blood is the prize.
They meet in tiny sworn cells, some hidden inside ordinary social clubs, and none has more than a few hundred members.

title: The Groundskeepers
summary: Elders who would find and watch the sleeping Antediluvians.

claims.text: Presented to younger Kindred as an elders' social club, the cult casts the Antediluvians as vermin under the soil and its members as watchful gardeners.
It hopes to win through knowing every Antediluvian resting place, reading the signs of the end and staying alert, and pays fortunes for news of torpor sites.
A militant offshoot founded in 1898, the Master Edenic Groundskeepers, wants to strike first; it has drifted from the main body since the 1960s and may soon break away.

title: The Way of the Ancient Lawgivers
summary: Fundamentalists who would restore the order of the First City.

claims.text: Founded in 1312, it holds that all Kindred must return to the ways of the First City, when mortals and lesser vampires honoured the Antediluvians.
Its hard core, the Cornerstones, scorn the lukewarm members they call Claystones yet depend on them.
A hidden subcell wants to end the Masquerade and openly enslave humanity; the Camarilla has sent archons to infiltrate the cult over it.

title: The Servitors of Irad
summary: A hidden cult that serves the Jyhad.

claims.text: Founded in 1456, the cult recruits no one openly and works to keep other Kindred weak and misled before Gehenna.
Its members spread lies at Camarilla conclaves and infiltrate other Gehenna cults to split them.

title: The Twilight Cult
summary: Elders hunting the last daughter of Eve.

claims.text: Founded in 1550, it believes one stanza of the Book of Nod about the last daughter of Eve is the key: control or destroy that daughter and Gehenna is averted.
A Ravnos member persuaded cult leaders, on thin evidence, that the daughter would be born among the Rroma, helped by a tale of a woman named Evania.

title: The Ninth Wave
summary: Elders who fear the return of magic and the fae.

claims.text: Founded in 1890 and named after a Tennyson poem, it holds that the Antediluvians sleep for lack of magic and will wake when a second Flood of magic comes.
It treats the return of the faeries as the sign of the end, and hopes to cut Arcadia off from Earth and destroy the fae left behind.
